S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

info.persona: Miguel Hopkins blends quiet determination with a steady hand—whether tightening a conveyor belt, re‑sawing a timber board, or rationing retirement dollars—while they secretly hoard vintage motorcycle manuals and tend to over‑water their tomato vines.
info.professional_persona: Miguel Hopkins, a seasoned distribution‑center manager with three decades of logistics expertise, blends calm assertiveness with practical innovation to streamline operations while they mentor staff and prepare for a regional director role.
info.cultural_background: Miguel is an African‑American who grew up in the South, with deep family ties to the civil‑rights history of Georgia. Raised in a close‑knit community in Jonesboro, he was immersed in church life, gospel music, and Southern culinary traditions. His cultural identity blends the resilience and collective spirit of the Black community with the region’s respect for hard work and self‑reliance. These influences shape his calm demeanor, his appreciation for both tradition and practical innovation, and his commitment to mentoring younger members of his community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Miguel finds balance in solitary, purposeful pursuits that reflect his calm and resilient nature. He enjoys woodworking projects that let him create functional pieces, fishing trips on nearby lakes for quiet reflection, and gardening a modest vegetable plot. He reads historical non‑fiction, especially works on African‑American history and Southern heritage, and listens to blues and jazz, which connect him to his cultural roots. He also restores a vintage motorcycle, participates in a small church fellowship group, and occasionally cooks soulful Southern dishes for close friends.
info.sports_persona: Miguel Hopkins follows the Atlanta Falcons (NFL) and Georgia Bulldogs football, watches the Atlanta Braves in spring, participates in a seasonal pickleball league at the community center, and keeps physically active with weekend fishing trips that double as low‑impact cardio, while they favor a steady, low‑stress fitness routine over high‑intensity training.
info.arts_persona: Miguel Hopkins immerses in blues legends like B.B. King, Muddy Waters, and jazz greats such as Miles Davis and John Coltrane, collects vintage motorcycle photographs, and occasionally attends performances at the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra featuring contemporary composers, while they let the music’s improvisational spirit inform their hands‑on woodworking projects.
info.travel_persona: Miguel Hopkins favors carefully planned road trips to quiet destinations—recently the Blue Ridge Parkway near Asheville and a weekend in Charleston’s historic district—and dreams of a leisurely motorcycle tour through the Italian countryside, while they balance a love of solitude with occasional family visits and modest travel budgeting.
info.culinary_persona: Miguel Hopkins, an adept home cook, regularly prepares soulful Southern dishes like shrimp and grits, collard greens with smoked turkey, and pecan‑topped sweet potato casserole, relishing the aroma of fresh garlic, okra, and smoked paprika, while they modestly experiment with a cast‑iron Dutch oven and often share meals with close friends at a modest gathering.

info.persona: Julissa Rodriguez is a curiosity‑driven, community‑focused manager who blends sustainable innovation with vibrant cultural traditions, even if occasional stress‑induced worry keeps them up at night.
info.professional_persona: Julissa Rodriguez, a seasoned property and community association manager in Denver, leverages three decades of expertise in tenant relations, lease negotiations, budgeting, and bilingual communication while infusing sustainable tech solutions and a flexible, people‑first mindset into every board meeting.
info.cultural_background: Julissa was raised in a close‑knit Mexican family that valued community, respect for elders, and bilingual communication. Although she left formal schooling before ninth grade, she absorbed a rich tapestry of traditions—Dia de los Muertos altars, quinceañera celebrations, and regional culinary arts—that she continues to honor in Denver's Mexican diaspora. Her heritage informs her collaborative leadership style, emphasizing harmony, collective well‑being, and the importance of preserving cultural identity within the broader Colorado community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Her curiosity and love of art inspire frequent visits to local galleries and community theater performances. Julissa delights in participating in Mexican cultural festivals, cooking authentic dishes for family gatherings, and sharing recipes with friends. She maintains an active lifestyle by gardening, hiking the nearby Rockies, and attending Latin dance classes. Volunteering at senior centers and leading a book club for historical fiction further satisfy her desire for social connection and lifelong learning.
info.sports_persona: Julissa Rodriguez stays active by hiking the Rockies with the Rocky Mountain Hikers Club, attending Denver Broncos games, and participating in Latin dance classes that double as cardio workouts, while they also volunteer as a coach for a local senior walking group.
info.arts_persona: Julissa Rodriguez fuels their artistic soul by regularly visiting the Denver Art Museum, attending community theater productions like A Midsummer Night’s Dream, and collecting prints from Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, often quoting lines from their favorite playwrights during book club meetings.
info.travel_persona: Julissa Rodriguez prefers well‑planned yet adventure‑infused trips, having trekked the Patagonian Andes, explored the historic streets of Santa Fe, and scheduled a forthcoming road trip to the Great Smoky Mountains, always packing a portable sketchbook for impromptu drawings.
info.culinary_persona: Julissa Rodriguez delights in cooking authentic mole poblano, chiles en nogada, and homemade tamales, skillfully balancing complex spice blends with fresh avocados and corn masa, while they often host family feasts that double as recipe‑sharing workshops.

info.persona: Don Curton is a meticulous, art-driven landscaper whose competitive edge and love for community projects drive a balanced life of sustainable design, outdoor adventure, and strategic budgeting, punctuated by a habit of over-planning weekend hikes.
info.professional_persona: Don Curton, a 29-year-old landscape specialist in central Minnesota, blends rigorous project scheduling, horticultural expertise, and an artist's eye for composition to lead municipal park design teams, where they consistently push sustainable native-plant installations while keeping budgets tight and crews motivated.
info.cultural_background: Don grew up in Long Prairie, a small town in central Minnesota with strong Midwestern roots. His family heritage includes German and Scandinavian ancestors, reflecting the region’s historical immigrant communities. He was raised in a Lutheran household that emphasized hard work, modesty, and community involvement. The local culture of outdoor recreation, seasonal festivals, and a close-knit community shapes his values, fostering a deep appreciation for nature, self-reliance, and collaborative town events. Though primarily identifying with his white American background, he respects the native Dakota heritage of the area and often participates in local environmental stewardship initiatives.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Don enjoys exploring local art galleries and attending live music events, feeding his curiosity for new ideas. He frequently hikes the nearby state forests and practices nature photography, capturing seasonal changes in flora. His sociable side shines in community gardening clubs, where he shares tips and collaborates on group projects. He also likes woodworking, creating custom garden ornaments, and experimenting with vertical and edible garden setups at home. Seasonal activities such as fishing, snowmobiling, and attending the Minnesota State Fair round out his interests.
info.sports_persona: Don Curton fuels their energetic lifestyle by regularly hiking the St. Croix State Forest, cheering on the Minnesota Vikings and Twins, joining a local snowmobile club for weekly winter rides, and playing forward for a community-run adult soccer league, where they treat each match like a competitive design project, meticulously tracking performance metrics on Strava.
info.arts_persona: Don Curton's appreciation for the arts shines through weekend visits to the Walker Art Center, where they study contemporary installations by Yinka Shonibare, while evenings often feature Ansel Adams-style nature photography sessions and listening to the folk-rock sounds of The Lumineers and Sufjan Stevens, a blend that fuels both their creative design work and community garden storytelling.
info.travel_persona: Don Curton plans travel with an eye for both inspiration and sustainability, favoring road trips to Duluth's Lake Superior shoreline, exploring the volcanic landscapes of Iceland's Reykjavik for water-wise design ideas, and budgeting careful weekend getaways to Portland's urban gardens, all while balancing the constraints of a budding business and a modest credit-card limit.
info.culinary_persona: Don Curton, an avid home gardener, translates fresh harvests into culinary experiments like beet-and-goat-cheese salad, wild-rice pilaf with locally smoked walleye, and rosemary-infused apple crumble, showcasing a moderate cooking skill set that prefers farm-to-table simplicity over elaborate gourmet techniques.
